reasoning: The extract is almost entirely about using the consultation to gather evidence and revise analysis. It says all analysis "will be revised as necessary in light of responses to the consultation and a final impact assessment will be produced". It also invites evidence on communication costs, business costs, firm-size effects and small and micro business impacts, and promises an updated small and micro business assessment. On equality, it says the departments "will continue to assess and monitor the implications of this policy on equality and diversity during and following implementation, and subsequent adjustments will be made as necessary." That is the closest thing to post-implementation monitoring, and it covers only equality. It also commits to keeping the separate Employment Tribunals and Employment Appeal Tribunal "under review". The "plans for using consultation" element is well covered, with a clear statement of what happens to the results: the final impact assessment. However, there are no success measures or outcomes to be measured, no plan to test or pilot the policy, no evaluation plan and no timetable. The monitoring of equality is vague and has no method, dates or publication commitment. The strongest counter-example to Level 0 is the equality monitoring line, which gives a weak indication of follow-up, so Level 1 is the fair reading. Level 2 would need defined outcome measures, a description of how they will be developed, and details of testing or an evaluation plan. Level 3 would also need a timetable and publication plans for the results.
